It Was Already Dobbs: Abortion Bans and Maternal Health
The Supreme Court’s decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization raised concerns that strict state abortion bans would worsen maternal health through delayed emergency care, restricted access to terminations, and reduced OB-GYN supply. Using claims data for nearly one million pregnancies among commercially and Medicaid-insured women from 2020 to 2024, I estimate the effect of these bans in a staggered difference-in-differences design using states that protect abortion rights as controls. Effects on routine care-receipt outcomes are small and precisely estimated; the adverse-pregnancy-outcome composite rules out effects larger than 3.5% of the pre-policy treated mean. Neither shifts in pregnancy composition nor changes in OB-GYN supply explain these results. These findings suggest telehealth abortion access may have absorbed much of the demand shock, while pre-ban restrictions had already limited the marginal effect of bans on downstream care.
Scheduled Presentation: SEA 2026


First Do No Harm: The Labor Market Consequences of a Physician Disciplinary Record
with Colleen Carey and Amanda Agan
Using a novel dataset of 70,000 state medical board disciplinary actions across more than 40 states (2008–2023), we provide the first evidence on how State Medical Board discipline affects subsequent physician careers. Most disciplined physicians continue practicing—often in a new state and supplying fewer claims—evidence that can inform the optimal design of state oversight and disciplinary actions.

title: Gabrielle Sorresso
text:
Gabrielle Sorresso
PhD Candidate, Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy


Hi, I’m Gabrielle — a 5th-year PhD candidate at the Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy. I’m an applied microeconomist studying health economics and gender. I use causal inference methods and large-scale administrative data, primarily healthcare claims, to examine how policy shapes maternal and infant health, fertility, and physician behavior.
I’m currently working on projects examining the Dobbs decision and its impacts on maternal and infant health and fertility, work recently recognized with the Horowitz Foundation’s Most Outstanding Project Award. I also have joint work with Colleen Carey and Amanda Agan on how state medical board disciplinary policy shapes physicians’ future provision of care, and with Sharon Sassler on gender wage gaps and spousal occupation.
